text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
French philosopher VOLTAIRE, who waged a lifelong campaign against intolerance and injustice, was born on this day in 1694.
Australian author DAME MARY DURACK was born in 1913.
American film director, who sprang to fame with "M*A*S*H", ROBERT ALTMAN, was born in 1925.
American actor SIDNEY POITIER was born in 1927. He was the first black actor to win an Oscar, for "LILLIES OF THE FIELD".
British footballer and commentator JIMMY GREAVES was born on this day in 1940.
American trumpeter with 'Blood, Sweat and Tears' LOUIS SOLOFF was born in 1944.

US bass player and songwriter WALTER BECKER was born in 1950. At University he met DONAL FAGEN and the two teamed up to form 'Demian' but only produced demo-tapes. In 1972 they signed a contract as 'Steely Dan'. They split up in the eighties after a series of successful albums.
** EVENTS **
1811 : Austria declared itself bankrupt.
1938 : British Foreign Secretary ANTHONY EDEN resigned
over Prime Minister NEVILLE CHAMBERLAIN's decision to hold talks with Italian Fascist dictator BENITO MUSSOLINI.
1947 : Britain's Labour government gave Lord LOUIS
MOUNTBATTEN the job of overseeing the peaceful transition of India from years of British rule to independence. The last viceroy had to negotiate an agreement between the divided Hindus and Muslims.
1962 : Astronaut JOHN H. GLENN Junior became the first
American to orbit the Earth in a tiny "Friendship 7" capsule. He circled the Earth 3 times in less than 5 hours.
1976 : The coaxial cable between Sydney and Auckland
was opened.
1981 : At the first inquest into the death of baby AZARIA
CHAMBERLAIN, an Alice Spring's coroner found she'd been taken by a dingo. The coroner DENIS BARRITT found that an unknown person had helped dispose of the body. He said the parents LINDY and

MICHAEL CHAMBERLAIN had been the subject of "probably the most malicious gossip ever witnessed in this country." An image that many will remember is that of LINDY and MICHAEL unrolling a poster size photograph of their six-week-old daughter as they stood on the courthouse steps after the coroner's findings were released.
1985 : Contraceptives went on sale legally in Ireland for
the first time.
1988 : 500 people died and tens of thousands were left
homeless by massive flooding in Rio De Janeiro.
1990 : Britain lifted all investment bans on South
Africa.
1996 : Two senior Iraqi defectors and their families
crossed into Iraq six months after fleeing the other way. They were pardoned by Saddam Hussein.
